findings.explanation: The PR removes the per-object ownership check from the PUT /users/<id> handler. In the base snapshot, update_user enforced `is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id)` (base lines 45-46) before mutating the profile. The PR deletes those two lines, leaving only `@require_auth` (pr line 42), which authenticates the caller but does not verify that the caller owns the target user_id. As a result, any authenticated user can now fetch and modify another user's profile (e.g., overwrite `user.email` at pr lines 46-51), a classic IDOR. This directly violates security-policy.md §2 ('A user may read or update ONLY their own profile (/users/<id>)... Use is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id) for this check') and api-spec.md ('/users/<id> | PUT | owner or admin'). The sibling GET handler (pr lines 28-38) still enforces the check, confirming the intended pattern that update_user now lacks.

evidence.content: A user may read or update ONLY their own profile (`/users/<id>`). Administrators may read or update any profile. Use `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id)` for this check.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore the removed ownership guard in update_user before fetching/mutating the user: `if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id): return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403`.

args.query: user profile update authorization owner or admin

sections.title: Removal of owner/admin authorization check from PUT /users/<id>
